# W3 handoff: git server and LFS

Workstream W3 of [`15-build-plan.md`](../../spec/15-build-plan.md), on branch `ws/w3-git-server`. Spec: [04](../../spec/04-git.md) and [`git-server-research.md`](../../research/git-server-research.md).

## Done, by feature ID

### UP-2: upload through `git push` with git-lfs

- `POST /{repo}[.git]/git-receive-pack` and `GET .../info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`, for models and `/datasets/...`.
- go-git v6 `transport.ReceivePack` unpacks into a private **push quarantine**: a bare directory whose `objects/info/alternates` lists the view's objects and, flattened, every alternate the view has. Refs live in memory (branches, tags and HEAD from the view's `packed-refs` and loose refs); `refs/pr/*`, `refs/convert/*` and `refs/hangar/*` are hidden from push.
- The pre-receive hook checks the policy, then calls `repo.Service.ApplyPack` with the received pack (verbatim, as go-git wrote it) and every ref update. On success it resets the in-memory refs to the old values, so go-git's own compare-and-swap succeeds and report-status says `ok`. The git server never writes refs or objects anywhere else.
- Policy in the hook, with messages git shows as `! [remote rejected] <ref> (<reason>)`:
  - Mirrors are read-only.
  - Only `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`; `refs/pr/*` is refused with a pull request hint; names must pass git's format and go-git's safety checks.
  - The default branch cannot be deleted.
  - Force-pushing the default branch: `AllowForce` is passed to `ApplyPack` when `git.allow_force_push` is set or the caller holds the admin Role on the Repo. The Role is checked as if the Token had admin scope (Repo and Namespace restrictions still apply), so an admin pushing with an ordinary write Token can force-push.
  - Every new ref target must exist ("missing necessary objects").
  - Non-LFS blobs over `git.max_blob_size` are refused, naming the file (found by walking the pushed trees) and telling the user to track it with Git LFS.
  - Packs over `git.max_pack_size`: refused with 413 before reading when `Content-Length` says so, and while reading for chunked bodies.
  - Every LFS pointer must name a stored, verified object of the same size (`repo.LFSStore.StatMany`); objects still being verified are polled for up to `lfs.verify_wait`.
  - Namespace quota on the pack size, through the optional `QuotaChecker`.
- `ApplyPack` errors map to refusals: `ErrRefConflict` gives "reference has changed concurrently, fetch first"; `PolicyError`, `ErrReadOnly`, `ErrProtectedRef`, `ErrLFSObjectMissing` and `ErrInvalid` give their messages; anything else gives "internal server error, the request ID is ...", with the cause only in the log.
- Auth (05-auth.md): anonymous pushes get `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Hangar"`; a caller who can read but not write gets 403; one who cannot read gets 404.
- git-lfs Batch API (`POST /{repo}.git/info/lfs/objects/batch`), used by git-lfs and by `huggingface_hub` uploads (HF-LFS-UPLOAD in `interface-coverage.md`):
  - Objects already stored and verified get no `actions` (UP-6 deduplication).
  - `basic`: a presigned PUT from `repo.LFSStore.PresignPut` where the store supports it for that size, otherwise a Hangar URL with a signed token that streams into `repo.LFSStore.Ingest` (SHA-256 and size checked before the object is visible).
  - `multipart` (Hugging Face's custom transfer, used by `hf lfs-enable-largefiles`) when the client offers it and an object is over `lfs.multipart_threshold`: `href` is a signed completion URL; `header` holds `chunk_size` and zero-padded part numbers mapping to presigned part URLs or signed Hangar part URLs. Part size is `max(16 MiB, ceil(size/10000))` rounded up to a MiB, so every object fits S3's 10,000 parts.
  - Every upload has a `verify` action (signed): it accepts the object if it is stored and verified, and otherwise re-hashes it with `repo.LFSStore.Verify`.
  - Every signed URL names the Repo UUID and the object or upload in its scope, expires after `lfs.upload_url_ttl`, and needs no `Authorization`, because Hugging Face clients send none on part PUTs and completions. Actions have `authenticated: true`, so git-lfs never adds credentials to presigned S3 requests.
  - Mirrors refuse uploads (403); quotas apply to the new bytes of a batch (507).
- `/locks*`: always 404 with `{"message": "Locking is not supported"}`, so git-lfs quietly turns lock verification off (checked in compat: no locking hint on push).

### DOWN-3: `git clone`, `git fetch` and `git lfs pull`, including shallow clones

- `GET .../info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` and `POST .../git-upload-pack` run `git upload-pack --stateless-rpc [--advertise-refs] <view>` on the view from `repo.Service.OpenView`, with `uploadpack.allowFilter=true`, `allowAnySHA1InWant=false`, `allowReachableSHA1InWant=true` and `uploadpack.hideRefs=refs/hangar/`.
- `GIT_PROTOCOL` comes from a well-formed `Git-Protocol` header (v0, v1 and v2); the `# service=` smart reply is omitted for v2, as git http-backend does. gzip request bodies are accepted.
- Output is streamed and flushed per write, never buffered. The subprocess gets a minimal environment (`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, an empty `HOME`), is killed when the client disconnects, has a wall-clock limit of `git.timeout`, and on Linux a CPU limit of the same length (`prlimit`).
- Read access uses `auth.ActionReadFiles`: anonymous callers are challenged with 401 (for missing Repos too, so names do not leak), callers without access get 404, gated Repos without approval get 403.
- LFS downloads: the batch answers only objects the Repo references (`repo.Service.LFSRefs`). Present objects get a presigned GET in `redirect` mode where the store supports it, and a signed Hangar URL otherwise (range requests, `HEAD`, `ETag`). Objects a Partial mirror does not hold go to the optional `PullThrough` hook, or get the per-object 404 "Not in arsenal. Pull this file with: hangar pull <repo> --include <path>, or clone with GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1".
- Renamed Repos are served at their old paths too (`repo.Service.Get` follows renames), including signed URLs issued before the rename.

### Telemetry

- Spans: `git.advertise_refs`, `git.upload_pack`, `git.receive_pack`, `git.pre_receive` and `git.update_refs` (11-observability.md "Git").
- Metrics: `hangar.git.push{outcome=ok|rejected|conflict|error}`, `hangar.git.pack.duration{service}`, and for LFS transfers through Hangar `hangar.download.bytes`, `hangar.download.files` and `hangar.upload.bytes` with `protocol=lfs`.
- Nothing logs or records tokens, signed URLs or `Authorization` headers; route templates are set for every request.

## Tests

Evidence is in the W3 report; commands:

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Unit and HTTP tests, with the git CLI, against `repotest` fakes (coverage 90 %) | `go test -race -cover ./internal/gitserver/...` |
| Fuzz targets: batch request parser, Repo path parser, `packed-refs` parser | `go test -run '^$' -fuzz FuzzParseBatch ./internal/gitserver/` (and `FuzzParseRepoPath`, `FuzzReadPackedRefs`) |
| Compatibility suite: real `git`, `git-lfs` and the `hf` multipart agent, two replicas, against every registered backend | `go test -count=1 -tags compat ./compat/git/` |
| Whole repository | `make lint test` |

`compat/git` covers: clone over protocol v0 and v2, `--depth 1`, `--filter=blob:none`, fetch and pull through either replica, datasets, push of branches and lightweight and annotated tags, deletes, force-push rules, `refs/pr/*` refused, push to a Mirror refused, concurrent pushes through two replicas (the loser gets "reference has changed concurrently" and recovers with `pull --rebase`), Commits made through `repo.Service` cloned with identical SHAs and pushed Commits read back through `repo.Service`, token as password, 401 prompts, 403 for read-only tokens, 404 for private Repos, LFS push with basic transfer through Hangar URLs and through presigned URLs (an S3 simulator that rejects requests with both a signature and `Authorization`), deduplication across Repos, `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1` clone then `git lfs pull --include`, the `hf` multipart transfer through Hangar part URLs and presigned part URLs, pointer pushes without objects refused, and large non-LFS files refused.

`internal/gitserver/gitservertest` starts the git server with the same middleware order as `cmd/hangar` and runs the git CLI with a clean configuration; both suites use it.

## Known gaps

- **git 2.39** is not in any matrix I ran; everything ran with git 2.54.0 and git-lfs 3.7.1 on macOS. `requests/w3.md` item 5 asks for a Debian 12 job.
- **`git push --atomic`** fails on the client because go-git does not advertise `atomic`, although every push is all or nothing. Document it in the user docs (W9).
- **LFS deduplication and private content:** an upload batch for an object stored anywhere in the Instance returns no actions, so a user who knows a SHA-256 can push a pointer to it into their own Repo and then download it. This is the usual trade-off of Instance-wide deduplication (UP-6); the security review in phase 3 should decide whether to require proof of possession for objects not already referenced by a Repo the caller can read.
- **CPU limit** is applied only on Linux (the container platform); elsewhere only the wall-clock limit applies.
- **go-git refname checks after the hook:** go-git re-validates ref names after the pre-receive hook. The hook applies the same checks (`ValidateRefName`, `Validate`, `IsSafe`) first; go-git also rejects some Unicode components that fold to `.` on HFS+, which the hook does not, so such a push would be applied by `ApplyPack` and then reported as `funny refname`.
- **Quota and Pull-through** are optional dependencies; until W1's quota helper and W6's Pull-through are wired, no quota is enforced by the git server and absent Mirror objects always get the 404 message.

## What the integration lead must wire

See [`requests/w3.md`](../requests/w3.md):

1. Mount `gitserver.Server.Git()` and `.LFS()` as `httpx.Protocols.Git` and `.LFS` in `cmd/hangar`, built with `gitserver.ConfigFrom(cfg)`, a `TempDir` on local disk, the real `repo.Service`, `repo.LFSStore`, `auth.Authz`, an `httpx.Signer` from the Instance key, and the telemetry tracer and instruments.
2. Classify the protocol before the authentication middleware writes a 401, so bad git credentials get a Basic challenge.
3. Register a real-backend file in `compat/git` once W2 is merged, so the suite runs against `internal/repo` with SQLite and Postgres (the file I used is in the W3 report).
4. `go mod tidy` will make `github.com/go-git/go-billy/v6` a direct dependency.
